turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung assured O-lan that he would see to it that their eldest son was married and that all her wishes for the family would be fulfilled.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid asked O-lan if there was anything else she needed and assured her that she would take care of Wang Lung with all the devotion and care she had shown O-lan.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan insisted that her eldest son should wed soon and that she would find peace only when she saw him settled with his bride.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he would do as she wished and asked her to rest, showing his nervousness and devotion.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan insisted that her eldest son needed to marry soon so that she could die in peace, knowing her family was secure and her son was settled with a good wife.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he would marry soon to ease her mind, his voice trembling slightly with nervousness.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would ensure their son married soon and that she should not worry, her voice filled with reassurance and a hint of optimism.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told her husband and son that she needed to see her eldest son married before her passing, her voice steady but tinged with a sense of urgency.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he understood her wishes and would arrange the marriage as soon as possible, his words filled with a mixture of nervousness and determination.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told her husband and son that she felt the end drawing near, but that seeing her son married would bring her peace and allow her to die without regret.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother and father that he would do everything in his power to make her wishes come true, his voice wavering but resolute.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she must not worry about such matters and that he would take care of everything, his voice filled with a reassuring optimism that sought to lift her spirits.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told her husband and son that she would see them wed and then she must die, her voice steady yet carrying a weight of inevitability.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother and father that he would find a suitable bride quickly and ensure the marriage took place without delay, his hands twisting nervously as he spoke.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told her husband and son that she felt the end approaching and that seeing her son married was her last wish, her voice steady but carrying a deep sense of urgency.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan and the eldest son that he would find the perfect bride for their son and that she must rest assured, her wish would be fulfilled, his tone filled with a mixture of optimism and determination.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung and their son that she felt the weight of her illness pressing down on her, but seeing her son married was her only comfort, urging them to move swiftly.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother and father that he would do everything in his power to make sure the marriage happened soon, his eyes filled with determination despite his nervousness.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung and their son that she would not rest until she saw her eldest son married, her voice firm and filled with a deep sense of responsibility for her family's future.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan and their son that he would speak to the maid and ensure the arrangements for the marriage were in place, his voice steady and reassuring.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she could not speak of dying and please him.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she must die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wed the good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served her, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe her face when she sweated in pain. Now she wanted her son to come home, because she must die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she could die easily, knowing her grandson was stirred into life and a great grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she would see him wed and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung to sit here and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung if everyone had wine and if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot and if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it and the eight fruits.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told her eldest son that she was now content and that he should look to his father and grandfather for guidance. She also instructed her daughter to observe her husband and his ancestors, pointing out the foolish woman in the court as an example of what not to do. O-lan insisted that her children had no duty to anyone else beyond these teachings.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung how that one could feed him and care for him as she did. Beauty would not bear a man sons!
